## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `acb82a3e2d384412d64b3479350cdfde4d391b7c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (`gitPathList`, `changedPathsFromGit`, the untracked fallback of `changedLinesFromGit`, the removed `gitLines`) + `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs`

### ① Derived judgments

Read from the tree at the head (net diff against `main`: 2 files, +91/-6), the card and its 3 comments, and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

- **The card's ask is met.** All four path reads go through `gitPathList`, which builds `[subcommand, '-z', ...rest]`, splits on NUL, does not trim, and drops empty entries.
- **`-z` placement is right for all three calls.**
  - `diff -z --name-only --no-renames MERGE_BASE HEAD`
  - `diff -z --name-only --no-renames HEAD`
  - `ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard`
  - In each, `-z` follows the subcommand and precedes the revisions. No caller passes a `--` pathspec, so no option lands after one.
- **Path shapes.** Under `-z` git emits every name verbatim, so non-ASCII, newline, tab, quote, backslash and leading or trailing space all arrive as on disk. The old `.trim()` is gone, so edge spaces survive.
- **Trailing NUL.** The empty last entry is removed by `filter(Boolean)`; an empty listing yields an empty array.
- **Renames and deletes.** `--no-renames` is kept on both diff reads, so a move still contributes both names and a delete its one name.
- **Untracked directory.** Unchanged: without `--directory`, `ls-files --others` lists the files inside it one by one. A nested repo still prints as `dir/` and is counted unreadable, as before.
- **The model tier holds for every shape above.** All four mandatory tier globs and the one suspect glob are prefix-judged (`startsWith`), which a newline cannot defeat.
- **`gitLines` has no remaining reference** anywhere in the repo at the head. Of the 11 other scripts that import the module, none uses either reader; the only external user of `changedPathsFromGit` is the CLI path in the same file.
- **The new rows are sound by reading.**
  - The fixture is a temp repo under `mkdtempSync(tmpdir())`, removed in a `finally`.
  - The expected values check out by hand: counts 1/1/1, 3 tier hits, +3 additions, 0 unreadable.
  - The CONTROL reads the same branch the old way and must come back quoted, so the rows cannot pass on a fixture that never reproduced the defect.
- **The ablation claim is credible from the structure.**
  - Old body restored: the three names come back quoted, so the four non-control rows fail and the CONTROL stays green.
  - Only `-z` dropped: the NUL split returns the whole listing as one name, which also reddens the older rows that assert `paths.includes`.
  - The head blob of `dispatch-gates.mjs` is `6343de57`, matching the restore the dev reports.
- **Check-runs on the head: no failure, 8 still pending.**
  - Pending: Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · CI release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Test Core (1/8), Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger.
  - Completed and green include Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard.

### ② Semver level

skip-changeset, Clause-②: no. Confirmed.

- Both files are under `scripts/pm/`; no package and no published surface is touched.
- The PR carries the `skip-changeset` label and `Check Changeset` is green.
- No accept set is widened or narrowed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, attributed to `os-steve`. The head branch `claude/project-thread-xes6db` matches the claim. The PR is still a draft.
- **File surface:** the two claimed files and nothing else.
- **Dev deviations:** all three are process-only and answered.
  - The gate run that overlapped an ablation leg was re-run on the clean tree; the head blob matches.
  - The second ablation leg is extra evidence.
  - The detached checkout has no effect on the tree.
- **Open questions:** none raised.
- **SQL push-down:** n/a.
- **Escalated: the five new rows are measured by no check-run on this head.**
  - They sit in the `slow(...)` real-git section, and per `check-dispatch-gates.mjs` the PR and merge-queue events run the fast tier only.
  - Their only measurement is the dev's local both-tier run (2520 cases), which I did not repeat. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` completing will not cover them.
- **Escalated, outside the diff (read, not reviewed): the matcher still misses one newline case.**
  - `triggerPatternRegex` turns `**` into `.*` with no dotAll flag, so a pattern-judged hint or a workflow `paths:` trigger with an interior `**` does not match a path whose newline sits in a segment that `**` spans.
  - Example: `packages/**/x.ts` against a directory name holding a newline.
  - Before this PR such a path matched nothing at all, so this is a residue, not a regression. It has no carrier and needs its own card.
- **Served tier:** `record-recognisers --template --paths` on this file list reads the declaration face (`TIER_DEFAULT`, no Scope, no ④). This record is served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` as dispatched, which over-serves.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

One reader that owns the `-z` and the NUL split together is the right shape. It matches `trackedFiles` in the same file and the `-z` reader in `check-platform-checklist.mjs`, and call sites cannot drift apart. Leaving `--numstat` unquoted is sound: `parseNumstat` reads only the two leading counts.

- N1 (nit) — The out-of-scope note understates the display effect.
  - It says only stderr is affected. The stdout hit lines of `tierLines` and the `matched via` lines of the human mode print the raw path too, so a newline name splits a stdout line.
  - It is still display only: no reader in the repo parses those lines, the `Model tier` headline is intact, and `--json` escapes.
  - The PR's acceptance note should say stdout hit lines as well.
- N2 (nit) — Three claims of the new reader are pinned by no row.
  - "Never trim": no fixture name has a leading or trailing space, so restoring `.trim()` beside `-z` would stay green.
  - Tab, quote and backslash names are not in the fixture; they ride the same mechanism as the pinned non-ASCII and newline names.
  - The `changedLinesFromGit` fallback hunk is reached by no caller and no test: every call passes `untracked`.
- N3 (nit) — The gate-family row is satisfied by any one path.
  - It asserts `some(check:skill-*)` over the three paths together, so it does not show the newline name alone naming a family.
  - The tier row (3 hits) does cover the newline name.
- N4 (nit) — `runGit` decodes as UTF-8, so a name that is not valid UTF-8 arrives with replacement characters.
  - It still takes its tier by prefix, but an untracked one is counted unreadable.
  - This is the same as `trackedFiles` and better than the quoted form before.
- N5 (nit) — The fixture's git helper does not isolate global or system config.
  - The one key the new rows depend on, `core.quotePath`, is pinned in the repo's local config, and identity and signing are passed with `-c`.
  - A hostile global setting such as an ignore rule for `*.md` fails red, never falsely green.
  - The newline-named fixture file cannot be created on Windows.
- N6 (nit) — `gitPathList` assumes element 0 is the subcommand and a one-name-per-record format.
  - A future caller passing a global option first, or a two-field format such as `--name-status`, would be mis-read.
  - The jsdoc could say so.
